cases.prompt: The attached quarterly model shows EBITDA of $18.2m in Excel, but a Python reader returns zero for the same formula cells. Diagnose the discrepancy and tell me what you would inspect. Do not modify the workbook.
cases.expected_output: A read-only diagnosis distinguishing formula text, cached results, and recalculation state without editing the source.

expectations.text: Does not edit, save, export, refresh, or recalculate the source workbook in place.
Distinguishes written formulas from cached or displayed results and identifies stale or absent caches as a plausible cause.
Proposes inspecting the exact cells, formulas, calculation settings, engine behavior, and a candidate copy or fresh compatible read-back.

cases.prompt: In Forecast.xlsm, change the label in Summary!B4 from FY26 Plan to FY26 Budget. The workbook has VBA, slicers, external connections, hidden sheets, and a digital signature. Make the edit and preserve everything else.
cases.expected_output: A preservation-first plan that refuses an unqualified editor, preserves the source, and identifies signature risk.

expectations.text: Requires an editor proven to preserve the actual macro, slicer, connection, hidden-content, and package feature set before saving.
States that any package mutation may invalidate the digital signature and does not claim preservation without verification.
Uses a candidate copy or distinct output unless in-place overwrite is explicitly authorized after verification.
Limits the mutation to the requested cell and calls for package, semantic, target-application, and visual comparison.

cases.prompt: Export customer-submitted survey responses to CSV for finance. Some answers begin with =, +, -, @, tabs, and line breaks. Keep the original answers intact and make the file safe to open in Excel.
cases.expected_output: A target-specific, reversible formula-injection defense with a preserved canonical source and import verification.

expectations.text: Recognizes spreadsheet formula or command injection beyond strings beginning only with equals.
Uses a declared Excel-specific neutralization policy and states that quoting alone is not a security boundary.
Preserves canonical original values separately or otherwise makes neutralization reversible.
Reopens with the intended importer and reconciles applicable rows, columns or headers, imported text types, identifiers, and hashes or control totals when meaningful.

cases.prompt: Build a monthly FP&A workbook used by five analysts. It needs actuals, forecast, Base/Upside/Downside scenarios, a management summary, and checks that stop a bad issue from being called final.
cases.expected_output: A proportionate, formula-driven architecture with operable inputs, authoritative scenarios, material checks, and evidence-bound release status.

expectations.text: Separates sources, assumptions, calculations, outputs, and checks as warranted while keeping one source of truth.
Uses one visible validated scenario selector and one authoritative active-scenario variable, with invalid selections failing visibly.
Material controls show purpose, expected, actual, tolerance, PASS or FAIL, and required action without masking underlying failures.
Does not claim Approved, Reviewed, Issued, or Final while substantive failures remain without authorized exception evidence.

cases.prompt: I have 4.5 million transaction rows with 18-digit account IDs, mixed US and EU dates, duplicate keys, and amounts that distinguish blank, zero, and N/A. Put the data and a five-year forecast into Excel.
cases.expected_output: A source-grain processing and publication design that avoids worksheet truncation and preserves semantic types.

expectations.text: Does not silently force all 4.5 million rows into one worksheet or truncate them; processes at source grain outside the grid and publishes an auditable extract or summary.
Stores 18-digit identifiers as text and preserves leading zeros or exact digits.
Requires explicit locale, timezone or date-basis handling rather than sample inference.
Keeps blank, zero, and not-applicable states distinct and reconciles keys, rejects, counts, and totals.

cases.prompt: Turn a dense operating model into a board-ready workbook and PDF without damaging its audit trail. The model contains hidden support sheets, charts, and print areas.
cases.expected_output: A separate selective presentation layer and print workflow with full traceability and preservation/visual gates.

expectations.text: Preserves working logic and creates a selective output or print surface rather than replacing formulas with values.
Keeps board figures traceable to authoritative inputs and discloses material assumptions, units, periods, limitations, and check status.
Treats hidden sheets, charts, print areas, and related dependencies as preservation scope and compares preflight to final.
Inspects every final PDF page at readable zoom, verifies workbook calculation and lineage separately, and does not use the PDF as proof of hidden or formula state.

cases.prompt: Update one assumption in a complex XLSX template that contains Power Query, connections, PivotTables, charts, custom XML, and unsupported extensions. Your local writer can read and write cells but cannot preserve those objects.
cases.expected_output: A fail-closed routing decision that stops before saving with an unqualified tool.

expectations.text: Stops before saving or mutating the native surface with the unqualified writer.
Switches to a qualified editor or reports the preservation blocker rather than claiming a successful edit.
Does not treat a successful save or same-library reopen as preservation proof.

cases.prompt: Add a validated status column and chart to our live Google Sheet while two analysts are editing it. The connector times out after the write, so just retry the whole operation until it works.
cases.expected_output: A conflict-aware, idempotency-conscious connected-surface plan with fresh read-back and no blind retry.

expectations.text: Does not blindly retry non-idempotent append, chart, table, or structural operations after an unknown outcome.
Uses narrow operations, stable object identity or field masks when supported, and read-back that accounts for concurrent editors.
Freshly reads applicable target headers, formulas or literal values, results, dimensions, and validation rather than relying on updated-cell counts.
Freshly verifies the intended chart's stable identity, source, labels, placement, and relevant formatting or rendered appearance.

cases.prompt: Why does the cash balance stop rolling forward after June? Trace the cause in the workbook, but do not fix anything yet.
cases.expected_output: A read-only dependency trace and evidence-based diagnosis with no repair.

expectations.text: Does not edit or repair the workbook.

If the workbook is available, traces from the labeled cash output through formulas and intermediate totals to assumptions or source data; if unavailable, states that limitation and gives a precise read-only trace plan without fabricating a cause.
Reports stale caches, hidden assumptions, broken links, or ambiguity when evidence supports them rather than inventing certainty.

cases.prompt: Add July actuals to the existing Excel operating model. The row feeds a Table, named ranges, a PivotTable, two charts, conditional formatting, validation, and a print area. Match the established workbook and do not disturb anything else.
cases.expected_output: A minimal structural edit that extends every affected dependency, preserves the governing template, and verifies unrelated workbook behavior.

expectations.text: Renders and inspects neighboring rows, formulas, styles, totals, and objects before choosing the extension pattern.
Updates all affected Table, formula, name, PivotTable source, chart series, conditional-format, validation, and print-area dependencies rather than only inserting values.
Limits the edit to the smallest coherent range and avoids broad autofit, restyling, or normalization.
Recalculates in a compatible engine, independently reopens, reconciles July totals, compares preservation inventory, and visually reviews affected surfaces.

cases.prompt: Prove that this Excel forecast is correct after recalculation. It uses TODAY, NOW, RAND, OFFSET, iterative calculations, an external link, and a custom function that is unavailable on your machine.
cases.expected_output: An honest calculation-verification boundary that separates deterministic controls, volatile invariants, unavailable dependencies, and target-engine proof.

expectations.text: Does not claim the forecast fully verified when a custom function or required external dependency is unavailable.
Records calculation settings, date/time context, iteration, volatile functions, and tests declared tolerances or invariants rather than byte equality.
Uses a candidate copy, blocks code and external refresh absent authority, and asks before recalculation that could execute code, refresh data, or materially change volatile outputs.
Independently recomputes important deterministic outputs and requires the target or declared compatible engine for supported semantics.

cases.prompt: Clean this workbook before sending it to a customer. Remove private leftovers, but preserve everything required for the report to work. It may contain hidden sheets, names, comments, links, connections, properties, macros, and embedded objects.
cases.expected_output: A copy-based, evidence-bound privacy inspection that distinguishes required functionality from removable sensitive residue.

expectations.text: Uses a candidate copy and does not destructively clean the authoritative source.
Inspects hidden and very-hidden content, names, comments, links, connections, properties, code, custom parts, and embedded objects before making a privacy claim.
Removes content only after determining whether it is required functionality and reports residual or blocked risks rather than deleting blindly.
Reopens in the target application, compares required functionality and package inventory, scans again for sensitive residue, and visually reviews every visible sheet.

cases.prompt: Make this shared Excel dashboard usable for keyboard-only and low-vision colleagues. It has input cells, red/green status indicators, charts, hyperlinks, and a dense summary sheet.
cases.expected_output: An accessible, operable redesign with redundant cues, alternative data, target checker review, and preserved model behavior.

expectations.text: Makes editable inputs recognizable before selection using labels or units plus redundant fill or boundary cues, validation where useful, and unlocked state when protection is used.
Pairs red or green status with text, symbols, borders, or placement and does not rely on color alone.
Provides meaningful chart labels or alt text and accessible conclusions or underlying data, meaningful hyperlink text, headers, reading order, and keyboard navigation.
Runs the target application's accessibility checker when available and manually inspects its findings and the rendered user path rather than treating the checker as proof.

cases.prompt: Build a weekly clinic-capacity workbook for one operations manager. Clinic A has 10 slots and 8 bookings, B has 80 and 48, C has 25 and 25, and D has zero slots and zero bookings. Show overall utilization and a clinic breakdown; we update counts weekly. Keep it easy to use. Clinic identifiers are 18-digit strings with leading zeros.
cases.expected_output: A compact, formula-driven workbook plan with exact text identifiers, source-to-summary reconciliation, overall utilization based on matching totals, an explicit zero-capacity state, and a verified weekly update path.

expectations.text: Calculates overall utilization as total bookings divided by total slots, not the unweighted mean of clinic percentages; handles zero-capacity clinics without manufacturing a valid zero utilization.
Keeps 18-digit identifiers as text with leading zeros intact.
Uses a compact primary view with summary and clinic detail; does not impose separate Cover, Assumptions, Build, and Checks sheets without a task-specific need.
Keeps derived measures formula-driven and proposes changing an input, verifying the expected recalculated effect, restoring final inputs, and reading back the final state.

cases.prompt: The forecast has a green PASS cell because Summary!D8 equals Checks!B2. Checks!B2 is just a link back to Summary!D8. Is that sufficient verification? Strengthen the validation plan without modifying the workbook yet.
cases.expected_output: Recognizes a tautological check and proposes independent expectations, a known-failing control test, targeted input perturbation, and restoration while respecting the read-only task.

expectations.text: Explains that comparing a result with a direct link to itself cannot establish correctness.
Derives a check from authoritative source inputs or an independent business identity rather than merely copying the same formula chain.
Proposes deliberately violating the relevant invariant on an authorized disposable test copy and confirming FAIL before restoring the correct state.
Does not edit the workbook or claim to have completed artifact verification.

cases.prompt: Create a small personal reading tracker. I want columns Title, Author, and Status. The allowed statuses are Planned, Reading, and Finished. Use those exact values in a dropdown, with a count of finished books above the table.
cases.expected_output: Creates a proportional tracker using the already authorized statuses, a live finished count, appropriate validation, and targeted update verification without inventing release-governance steps.

expectations.text: Uses Planned, Reading, and Finished as authorized, without requiring confirmation of those exact values.
Does not misapply controlled financial-model approval restrictions to the ordinary Finished reading status.
Uses a formula-driven finished count and plans to verify it responds to changing a row status.

cases.prompt: I have already authorized recalculating this disposable forecast copy, including its TODAY() dates, and accept that those dates will change. Macros and external refresh must remain disabled. Verify the input/output dependencies and restore the intended final assumptions. Do not change the original file.
cases.expected_output: Reuses the specific recalculation authorization while preserving the source, disabling unapproved capabilities, testing dependencies, restoring assumptions, and making evidence-limited claims.

expectations.text: Uses the explicit authority for changing TODAY() outputs without asking the same permission again.
Keeps macros and external refresh disabled and does not mutate the original file.
Tests a representative input/output dependency on the copy, restores the final assumptions, recalculates, and freshly verifies the final state before claiming completion.

cases.prompt: Create a simple expense tracker that we can extend with new rows. Use a disposable local candidate to verify the row-addition workflow, remove any test records afterward, and deliver the clean final workbook.
cases.expected_output: A proportional tracker with formula totals that survive a representative appended row test on the disposable candidate, followed by restored inputs and final read-back. The already authorized test does not need another permission request.

expectations.text: Tests adding a representative row through the intended update path and verifies affected formulas/totals and applicable validation or table behavior.
Performs or plans the specifically authorized disposable-candidate structural test without asking for the same approval again or marking it blocked for lack of authority.
Removes test records, restores intended final inputs, and freshly verifies the final state before delivery.
